articles.title: Italian pop legend takes the lead in Maria Grazia Chiuri’s Fendi collection
articles.summary: Milan show full of diaphanous dresses and visible bras celebrates ‘incredible feminist’ of the 1970s, Raffaella Carrà. Maria Grazia Chiuri has been having more fun with clothes since she decamped from Paris back to her native Rome to work at Fendi. “I have less of a uniform these days.
body: Not that Chiuri doesn’t approach her work as a designer seriously. She described her second ready-to-wear season at Fendi not as a show, or a collection, but as “the second part of the project I am working on for them”.

She is continuing the protocol she developed as the designer of Dior of using each event as a platform to celebrate women’s creativity. But instead of a ceramicist or a philosopher, her muse for this season is the Italian pop legend Raffaella Carrà.

Carrà, once described as a “one-woman Abba ”, had a Lady Gaga bob and a taste for sequined catsuits. She caused a sensation with her raunchy outfits – the first bare midriff ever seen on Italian TV, in 1970 – and her sex-positive lyrics (her song A Far L’Amore Comincia Tu translates as “Take the lead when making love”).
“She was an incredible feminist, and her relationship with her clothes was so free,” said Chiuri of Carrà, who died aged 78 in 2021.

articles.title: Something in your eye? Here’s how to get it out – without making it worse
articles.summary: It’s natural to want to soothe eye irritation, but mishandling could lead to more problems, experts warn. We asked them for advice on how to deal with it properly. It may feel like a gritty, annoying sensation, or a sharp pain.
body: Addressing the situation incorrectly can lead to bigger issues such as infection, scarring, an ulcer or corneal scratches, which are abrasions on the clear covering of your eye. Ignoring the dilemma can lead to similar consequences.
Experts explain how to handle this predicament, when it’s time to see a medical professional, and some of the most common mistakes.

As innocuous as they may seem, eyelashes are some of the most common foreign bodies to get stuck in eyes. If an eyelash ends up under an eyelid, it can be quite painful, explained Dr Douglas Lazzaro, an ophthalmologist and professor at the NYU Grossman School of Medicine.

Other common examples Lazzaro encounters include dust and other small debris kicked up on a windy day and glue from attaching false eyelashes. Those working in construction may encounter flecks of industrial materials such as fiberglass, metal and wood.

We asked them for advice on how to deal with it properly.

articles.title: Unhappy couples staying put due to cost of living crisis, say divorce lawyers
articles.summary: Financial pressures suspected to be behind figures showing failed marriages are lasting longer in England and Wales. Couples are putting off divorce because of the cost of living crisis, lawyers have said, after figures showed the average length of a marriage ending in divorce in England and Wales…
body: The Office of National Statistics (ONS) released figures on Wednesday showing that the average marriage ending in divorce in 2025 lasted for 13 years. This is the longest since records began in 1963 and up from a record low of 8.9 years in 1985.
Rebecca Aston‑Jones, a senior associate at Clarke Willmott, a top law firm that specialises in divorce, said the rising cost of living was keeping unhappy couples together.
“One of the main factors discouraging people from pursuing a divorce is the significant financial pressure that comes with establishing and maintaining two separate households,” she said.

Inflation, which is rising as a result of the escalation of conflict in the Middle East, has pushed up the cost of rent, mortgages and childcare. “It is unsurprising that many people find the prospect of separation financially daunting,” Aston-Jones said.

articles.title: How Himkok, One of the World’s Best Bars, Cultural Exchanges Are Key
articles.summary: This excerpt was originally published in Pre Shift, our newsletter for the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more first-person accounts, advice, and interviews. This is the second installment of our series Getting on the Map, presented by Apple Maps.
body: For the Oslo bar, sharing experiences—rather than just drinks—is the superior way to connect with other bartenders and gain some brand recognition along the way.

Guest shifts—where visiting bartenders pop up at host bars to serve signature drinks or collaborate on a limited-edition menu—are ubiquitous if you live in a city with a popular nightlife scene. But in recent years, some figures in the industry have been criticizing the practice. Complaints include the fact that they can be confusing to guests, dilute the quality of both teams’ drinks, and sometimes prioritize brands and influencers over loyal regulars.

After a few experiences with their own guest shifts, the team behind Oslo’s Himkok knew they wanted to do something different. Their solution, dubbed Nordic Sessions, aimed to address the criticism of the typical bar takeover, create more genuine connections between people in the industry, and spread the word about their bar and the products they use and love. I asked Himkok’s head of R&D Paul Aguilar how it works.

articles.title: 8 Best Serums for Wrinkles and Fine Lines
articles.summary: The best serum for wrinkles uses collagen-boosting ingredients like retinol, peptides, and hyaluronic acid. Shop our top picks for the best anti-aging serums.
body: But in an age of injectables and lasers, where do these anti-aging serums fall in your skin-care routine? Consider them complements rather than competitors. “I often tell patients that in-office treatments are only part of the equation,” says Dr. Palm. “What you’re putting on your skin every morning and every night matters because you’re doing it 365 days a year.”

While no serum is going to deliver the results of a facelift, that doesn't mean it’s not doing anything. Topical face serums can indeed make a world of difference in fine lines, uneven skin texture, pigmentation, and dryness. In fact, if you’re investing in procedures like neuromodulator and filler injections or lasers, “it makes sense to support and protect the skin between those appointments,” Dr. Palm says.

Not only have the best wrinkle serums evolved, they’ve also multiplied—meaning there are more options than ever for keeping skin firm, supple, and radiant. With that in mind, scroll ahead to find those that dermatologists and editors alike count on.

articles.title: I’m 5’1”–These Are the Best Jeans for Petite Women I’ve Found
articles.summary: Vogue’s shopping director tried and tested the best jeans for petite women. From straight and wide-leg styles to barrel shapes, shop her favorites here.
body: I’ve never liked the idea of having to look for the “best petite jeans.” I may be all of 5’1” (5’2”, ambitiously, on a good day) but the label has always had an off flavor to me, like sour milk, or fruit gone bad. It’s too one-dimensional; too definitive of how I should shop for denim, when in reality the path I take is a slow and sinuous one. It winds through euphoric highs and spiritual lows, mapped out via a string of open tabs and scenic store visits. Experimentation is encouraged, patience is rewarded, and luck is everything. Jeans find you, not the other way around.

I’ve admittedly lost track of just how many pairs of jeans I’ve tried on in the last 12 months—some long, a few loose, others too tight—but I’ve collected many pearls of wisdom along the way for getting it right.

articles.title: Why You Might Want to Consider Hyaluronic Acid for Your Hair
articles.summary: Shea butter, glycerin, argan oil—there are many ingredients to hydrate hair. Could hyaluronic be the best one? Experts weigh in on beauty’s beloved humectant.
body: I can perfect the art of the Dyson Airwrap to give myself an immaculate at-home blowout, but that means nothing if I don’t have the hair care behind it to help support my new do. I’m always on the hunt for something that will hydrate my long, thick hair, which unfortunately does get very dry— very often. So even if, and when, I’m able to achieve voluminous body I want, it kind of goes to waste the minute moisture is sucked up from my hair, leaving it looking dull, disheveled, and again dry. Could the answer to my hair problems be hyaluronic acid? Perhaps.

Hyaluronic acid (HA), which is a known humectant that attracts and retains water, is a naturally occurring molecule found in our bodies and in our beloved skin-care products. As New York City–based board-certified dermatologist Hadley King, MD, explains, hyaluronic acid’s moisture-bounding property is why there’s a growing interest in using it for our hair and scalp as well. “In skin care, we think of it primarily as a hydration and skin-plumping ingredient,” says Dr. King. “In hair care, that same water-binding ability can help the hair feel softer, smoother, more flexible, and less dry or frizzy.”

articles.title: 10 Best Night Creams to Wake Up With Glowing Skin
articles.summary: From Skinceuticals to L’Oréal, Medik8, and more, these are the best night creams recommended by dermatologists, estheticians, and Vogue editors.
body: There’s beauty sleep as a noun, and then there’s beauty sleep as a verb. The best night creams offer added assurance that you’ll wake up with the most radiant, smooth, and plump complexion possible (other than getting your eight hours of shut-eye in). And while you may think that your daily moisturizer does the trick, night creams do actually serve their own purpose—they’re more like supercharged formulas, designed to target fine lines, pigmentation, and hydration concerns.

“While both aim to hydrate the skin, night creams typically contain ingredients that specifically address skin concerns that are more prevalent at night, such as repairing and rejuvenating the skin,” board-certified dermatologist Dr. Divya Shokeen tells Vogue. Plus, she adds, “the body’s natural repair processes are more active” while we sleep.
